summary: Cognition now says it "may use Customer Data for model training purposes"; "paid Service Tier" customers "may opt out" (Teams administrator only).
"Train our models" became "train and improve Anthropic AI models", and research on the societal impacts of AI became a stated purpose.
xAI's enterprise terms dropped automatic 30-day deletion of User Content and claimed ownership of de-identified data for any lawful purpose.
Grok added a provision stating that it "shall not use any Google Apps content" connected via Google OAuth for "any of its internal AI or other training purposes."
OpenAI now says, "if training is enabled" or "if you provide feedback," it uses content, and also uses "data from third-party partners" to train models.
GitHub now says it may train on “Your Content” and Affiliates may use Inputs/Outputs “Unless you opt out,” replacing “if you allow in your settings.”

DeepSeek now states that "certain entities within our corporate group" process your provided, automatically collected and third-party data for "foundation model training and optimization"; the opt-out remains.
OpenAI now says “By default, data from ... ChatGPT for Healthcare ... isn't used for training ... unless you have explicitly opted in.”
DeepSeek still may train on Personal Data, but now grants “the right to opt-out of using your Personal Data for training our models or optimizing our technologies.”
Claude.ai (Anthropic) added use of Materials “to develop other products and services, including training our models,” “unless you opt out of training through your account settings.”
OpenAI now says “By default, we do not train… on any business data accessed from connectors,” replacing “We do not train…”
Anthropic still says it may use “Inputs and Outputs” to train “unless you opt out through your account settings”; it adds “Legitimate interests” language.
Microsoft now states that "in certain markets, we use conversation data to train the generative AI models in Copilot, unless you choose to opt-out of such training."
Jasper still may use Customer Property for “modifying, improving, and enhancing artificial intelligence models,” but EU/UK users “may have the right to object.”
Anthropic's Claude.ai now uses Materials for "training our models, unless you opt out of training through your account settings," with feedback and safety-flagged content trained on regardless.
Claude.ai (Anthropic) now says it “may use your Inputs and Outputs to train our models…unless you opt out through your account settings,” with safety-review/reported-materials exceptions.
xAI dropped its limit on training "only with the Usage Data you voluntarily choose to provide to us."
Grok (xAI) now says logged-in users “can select whether or not” User Content trains models; logged-out use “where permitted” grants “full rights” for training.
Microsoft still says it "may use your data to develop and train our AI models," but now states "Xbox's AI-enhanced features do not use children's data for model training."
Cursor (Anysphere) says “We do not use Inputs or Suggestions to train our models unless” flagged for security review, explicitly reported, or “explicitly agreed.”
Cursor replaced its Privacy Mode clause with: Anysphere will not train, or let any third party train, AI models on your content unless you explicitly agree.
Definitions reworded; the email route to opt out was removed
Pro users' no-training limits were made to override the general usage rights.
DeepSeek now says it may use “publicly available information via the Internet sources” “to train our models,” while still training on interactions/usage.
GitHub Copilot says Free users’ data “may be used for AI Model training where permitted and if you allow in your settings.”
OpenAI now says it “may use Content” to train “models that power ChatGPT,” rather than “models that power our Services,” unless you opt out.
OpenAI now says it uses Content to train models powering “our Services,” not just “ChatGPT,” with an opt-out for Content.
